01-enzymes.q: An enzyme is best described as…
options: a living organism that digests food
01-enzymes.explain: Enzymes are proteins that speed up reactions without being used up — biological catalysts.

01-enzymes.q: A catalyst…
options: is used up during the reaction
increases the rate of a reaction and is not used up
01-enzymes.explain: Both halves are needed for the two-mark definition: increases the rate, not used up.

01-enzymes.q: Enzymes are made of…
01-enzymes.explain: Enzymes are proteins, which is why heat and pH can change their shape.

01-enzymes.q: The part of an enzyme that the substrate binds to is the…
01-enzymes.explain: The active site has a shape complementary to the substrate.

01-enzymes.q: Why does each enzyme act on only one substrate?
options: Enzymes are too small to hold more than one
Only one substrate has a shape complementary to the active site
Each enzyme is used up after one reaction
01-enzymes.explain: This is specificity — the lock-and-key fit.

01-enzymes.q: When a substrate is bound in the active site, the structure formed is called…
01-enzymes.explain: Enzyme + substrate bound together = enzyme–substrate complex.

01-enzymes.q: What happens to an enzyme at the end of the reaction it catalyses?
options: It is broken down into amino acids
It becomes part of the product
It is unchanged and can be used again
01-enzymes.explain: A catalyst is not used up.

01-enzymes.q: Increasing the temperature from 10 °C to 30 °C speeds up an enzyme reaction because the molecules…
options: have more kinetic energy and collide more often
change the shape of the active site
01-enzymes.explain: Below the optimum the explanation is kinetic energy and collision frequency — the answer the 2023 teacher said students left out.

01-enzymes.q: The optimum temperature of most human enzymes is about…
01-enzymes.explain: Body temperature.

01-enzymes.q: Above its optimum temperature, an enzyme stops working because…
options: the substrate becomes too hot to move
01-enzymes.explain: Heat breaks the bonds holding the shape, so the substrate no longer fits. The enzyme is denatured, not dead.

01-enzymes.q: Which word describes an enzyme whose active site has permanently changed shape?
01-enzymes.explain: Denatured — and it does not recover when cooled.

01-enzymes.q: An enzyme is heated to 80 °C and then cooled to 37 °C. It will…
options: work at its normal rate again
not work, because denaturing is permanent
01-enzymes.explain: Denaturing cannot be undone by cooling.

01-enzymes.q: An enzyme kept at 4 °C and then warmed to 37 °C will…
01-enzymes.explain: Cold only slows molecules down; it never changes the shape of the active site.

01-enzymes.q: A rate–temperature graph for an enzyme usually…
options: rises gradually, peaks, then falls steeply
01-enzymes.explain: Gradual rise from kinetic energy, steep fall from denaturing.

01-enzymes.q: Pepsin works in the stomach. Its optimum pH is about…
01-enzymes.explain: The stomach contains hydrochloric acid.

01-enzymes.q: Moving an enzyme to a pH far above its optimum will…
01-enzymes.explain: Too alkaline denatures an enzyme just as too acidic does.

01-enzymes.q: Amylase breaks down starch into…
01-enzymes.explain: Amylase makes maltose. Maltase then makes glucose — two steps.

01-enzymes.q: Maltase breaks down maltose into…
01-enzymes.explain: The second step of starch digestion.

01-enzymes.q: Which enzyme breaks down protein?
01-enzymes.explain: Protease — pepsin is the protease in the stomach.

01-enzymes.q: The products of protein digestion are…
01-enzymes.explain: Proteins are chains of amino acids.

01-enzymes.q: Lipase breaks down lipids into…
01-enzymes.explain: Both products are needed for the mark.

01-enzymes.q: Which substance digests fat?
01-enzymes.explain: Asked as a one-mark table gap in Year 10 2024 Q1(c).

01-enzymes.q: Why can humans not release energy from cellulose?
options: Cellulose is denatured by stomach acid
01-enzymes.explain: Only cellulase has an active site that fits cellulose.

01-enzymes.q: Cellulase digests cellulose into…
01-enzymes.explain: The glucose is then used in respiration — the Year 11 January 2023 mock chain.

01-enzymes.q: Iodine solution turns blue-black in the presence of…
01-enzymes.explain: Iodine is the starch test.

01-enzymes.q: In the amylase practical, the reaction is complete when the iodine…
01-enzymes.explain: Orange-brown means no starch left.

01-enzymes.q: In an amylase experiment, a shorter time for the starch to disappear means…
01-enzymes.explain: Rate and time are inversely related.

01-enzymes.q: Starch disappears in 40 s at pH 6, 20 s at pH 7 and 55 s at pH 8. The optimum pH is about…
01-enzymes.explain: The shortest time is the fastest rate.

01-enzymes.q: In an investigation into the effect of pH on amylase, the independent variable is…
01-enzymes.explain: The thing you change.

01-enzymes.q: In an investigation into the effect of pH on amylase, the water bath is used to…
01-enzymes.explain: Temperature is a control variable here.

01-enzymes.q: Which is a valid control variable in an enzyme and temperature experiment?
options: Time taken for starch to disappear
01-enzymes.explain: Temperature is the independent variable and time is the dependent one.

01-enzymes.q: Why are samples taken every 10 seconds in the amylase practical?
options: To find the time when starch is no longer present
01-enzymes.explain: Regular sampling pins down when digestion finished.

01-enzymes.q: A reaction stops although temperature and pH are unchanged. The most likely reason is that…
options: the substrate has been used up
01-enzymes.explain: No conditions changed, so do not reach for denaturing.

01-enzymes.q: All the active sites are occupied and the rate is at its maximum. Which change would increase the rate?
01-enzymes.explain: The enzyme is the limiting factor.

01-enzymes.q: The chemical reactions in living cells, controlled by enzymes, are called…
01-enzymes.explain: Metabolism.

01-enzymes.q: Snails grow faster at 23 °C than at 8 °C. The best explanation is…
options: molecules have more kinetic energy so collisions are more frequent
01-enzymes.explain: The 2023 scheme rewarded kinetic energy and collisions; the teacher warned against the 'optimum loop'.

01-enzymes.q: Bile helps pancreatic enzymes work in the small intestine by…
01-enzymes.explain: Pancreatic enzymes have an alkaline optimum.

01-enzymes.q: In a six-mark investigation design, 'keep everything else the same' scores…
options: nothing — each control must be named
01-enzymes.explain: Name them: temperature, volume of amylase, mass of starch.

01-enzymes.q: Which statement about denaturing is correct?
options: The active site changes shape so the substrate no longer fits
The substrate changes shape to fit
01-enzymes.explain: Be specific: the active site.

01-enzymes.q: In the mock scheme for the vinegar investigation, which word for the starch was ignored?
01-enzymes.explain: 'Amount' is too vague. Say mass or volume.
